title: A film argues one claim at a time
statement: Build a short film on a text as a voiced argument, one visible claim at a time: the key line quoted exactly, what it shows, then two defensible readings.
detail: The video tool's style research inspected a 144-frame storyboard of a reference unit video and named its repeatable pattern one visible claim at a time, paced by voice (`g9/tools/unit-video-essay/INTEGRATION.md`). The lesson engine adopted it as its video essay: the writer is asked for the line that matters most, what it shows, and two readings a careful reader could defend, and a code check holds any essay whose first part is not a quotation (`g9/transformer/src/mechanics/video-essay.js`).
against: It is a design inference, not a measured effect: "That is a design inference from the sampled motifs." (g9/tools/unit-video-essay/INTEGRATION.md line 14). Nothing measures what students learn from a film built this way.

evidence.quote: The repeatable pattern is **one visible claim at a time, paced by voice**.
A 144-frame storyboard sampled at about 4.9-second intervals was inspected.
